notes: The spec asked geometry() to refuse planes narrower or shorter than native allows. Native accepts every size: check_params only warns and clips radius/radiusV to (plane-1)/2, down to radius 0 at 1x1 (probed with the sandbox reference, exit 0). The port therefore clips exactly as native does and the matrix compares sizes 1x1 and 2x2 and sizes near 2r+1 byte-exactly; the only size refusal is the uint16 luc wrap for planes wider than 65534 - radius, which has no native comparison.

t is the native formula (int)((2*r*rv + rv + r) * 2.f * percentile), i.e. ((2r+1)(2rv+1)-1) * percentile in float32, not percentile*(2r+1)*(2rv+1) as the spec summarised; percentile=1 selects the window maximum.
Native slice threading cannot change the result (nb_threads <= planeheight[1]/(radiusV+1) keeps every slice start inside the plane); verified against native default threads and -filter_threads 1.
Each filtered plane allocates a transient 544*width byte histogram scratch outside maxFrameBytes, as native allocates per thread.
No linux-gated cases: integer histograms plus one float32 product, run on every platform.

Setup: the sandbox had Node 22.23.5; the bootstrap requires Node 24, installed v24.22.3 with `n` in about 4 s. Bootstrap 193.7 s (npm 7.7 s, submodule 5.8 s, reference 180.2 s). Baseline typecheck+lint+boundaries+registry test 58 s, green. The reference differs from the linux-x64 pin, as expected with --allow-unpinned-reference.
